text:
Vancouver arrives winless in ten (0-9-1), outscored 45-20 over that stretch, after a 4-2 home loss to Minnesota on Sunday in which Quinn Hughes reached 500 career points. Anaheim has been just as shaky, 1-4-0 in its last five, but snapped a five-game winless run by coming back from two goals down to beat Philadelphia 5-4. The Ducks are home after a four-game road trip, still without Ryan Poehling and Pavel Mintyukov. Leo Carlsson has taken Poehling's spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn, and Nikita Klepov is up to 14:03 a night from 10:03.

The numbers favor Anaheim. At five on five, the Ducks have taken 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 38% for the Canucks, and our model projects 3.67 goals for ANA to 2.83 for VAN. Anaheim's power play also creates more, 0.65 expected goals a game to 0.44. In net, projected starter Kevin Lankinen is 12.3 goals worse than expected this season, and last year was 20.3 worse. Projected Ducks starter Lukas Dostal is 1.7 goals better than expected this year after 3.7 worse in 2025-26.

Watch Cutter Gauthier, who is 40% to score and has gone eight games without a goal despite 2.8 expected goals, and Carlsson, 79% for a point. For Vancouver, Elias Pettersson has a four-game point streak. Among our under-the-radar picks, Judd Caulfield, a third-liner with 2.5 expected goals in his last nine games, is 20% to score, and Mikael Granlund is 67% for a point. Both are players to watch, not locks.
